title: SIR Epidemic and Herd Immunity
summary: A town of ten thousand people, with {vaccinated:%} vaccinated. Each infected person passes the infection on at a rate that makes R0 = {R0} new cases in a fully susceptible town, and stays infectious for about {days} days. Model assumptions: everyone mixes evenly, recovery gives lasting immunity, the town is closed, and the hospital line is compared with everyone infected at once, as if each case needed a bed.

sources.title: Kermack and McKendrick, A contribution to the mathematical theory of epidemics (1927)
Fine, Eames and Heymann, Herd Immunity: A Rough Guide (2011)

params.label: Hospital line
params.help: How many people can be sick at once before care runs short.

derived.cells: fill(round(V / N * 100), 'V') + fill(round(R / N * 100), 'R') + fill(round(I / N * 100), 'I') + fill(max(0, 100 - round(V / N * 100) - round(R / N * 100) - round(I / N * 100)), 'S')

tick: let infections = R0 / days * S * I / N * dt
if not peaked and I > startI and nextI < I {

narration.text: The outbreak starts with {startI} infected people. Each passes it to {Reff:.2} others on average, because only {S / N:%} of the town can still catch it. Each square is one percent of the town.
Infected now: {I:int}. Effective R is {Reff:.2}. When it drops below one, new cases fall behind recoveries and the curve turns.
The outbreak fades. {S / N:%} of the town never caught it: the infection ran out of people to reach.

claims.text: An outbreak grows only when R0 times the share still susceptible is above 1.
The infection curve turns over when the susceptible share has fallen to 1/R0: from then on, each case causes less than one new case.
With {vaccinated:%} vaccinated, the number sick at once never passes the hospital line of {beds}.

claims.expr: abs(S - S0 * exp(-R0 * R / N)) < 0.01 * N
claims.text: How many have recovered fixes how many can still catch it: S = S0 × e^(−R0 × R / N) at every moment, Kermack and McKendrick's law, to within one percent of the town.
The outbreak burns out before the run ends, and people are left who never caught it.
